prompt.context_jp: テーコー不動産新宿営業所に、見慣れない女性客（＿）ふらりと姿を見せた。
prompt.prompt_jp: テーコー不動産新宿営業所に、見慣れない女性客＿ふらりと姿を見せた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces a new, previously unknown person into the scene.

feedback.correct_en: The woman is being introduced for the first time — new information — so が marks her as the newly appearing subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat her as an already-known topic, which doesn't fit a first appearance. を doesn't work with 姿を見せた here (姿 already takes を).

contrast_examples.jp: 知らない人が入ってきた。
contrast_examples.en: An unknown person came in. (new info)
As for that person, he came in. (already known)

prompt.context_jp: 課長の屋代＿まだ、自分の過去が扉を開けて入ってきたことに気づいていなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 課長の屋代＿まだ、自分の過去が扉を開けて入ってきたことに気づいていなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Yashiro as the topic of this sentence.

feedback.correct_en: Yashiro has just been introduced in prior sentences; now the narrator comments about him as the established topic, so は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce him as new info, which contradicts the discourse. に doesn't match the subject role.

contrast_examples.jp: 屋代は気づいていなかった。

prompt.context_jp: 課長の屋代はまだ、自分の過去＿扉を開けて入ってきたことに気づいていなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分の過去＿扉を開けて入ってきた
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle inside the subordinate clause describing what entered.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a subordinate clause (…ことに気づく), the embedded subject typically takes が, and 過去 is new information here.
feedback.incorrect_en: は tends to be reserved for the main-clause topic, not an embedded subject describing a new event.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が来たことを知らない。
contrast_examples.en: He doesn't know that she came.
As for him, he has come before.

prompt.context_jp: 「白洲美加の仕事は何だ？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 家＿売ることです
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the direct object of 売る.

feedback.correct_en: 売る takes a direct object, so 家 is marked with を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 家 the subject of 売る, which inverts the meaning. に marks a destination, not an object.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家の決めゼリフ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 私に売れない家＿ありません
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits her signature declaration.

feedback.correct_en: With negative-existence 〜はありません, は marks the topic/scope: 'as for houses I can't sell, there are none.' It gives the categorical, boastful tone of her tagline.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would merely assert existence/non-existence neutrally and lose the sweeping, topic-level claim that makes this her catchphrase.

prompt.context_jp: 布施＿担当する狛江の物件の売れ行きが低迷しているせいか、資料をめくる手つきもどこか上の空だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 布施＿担当する狛江の物件の売れ行きが低迷している
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Fuse as the topic whose situation is being described.

feedback.correct_en: Fuse is the established character being commented on; は sets him as topic, and inside the clause 売れ行き takes its own が.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce Fuse as new information, but he's already a known character here.

contrast_examples.en: He is the one who got the job.

prompt.context_jp: 布施は担当する狛江の物件の売れ行き＿低迷しているせいか…
prompt.prompt_jp: 売れ行き＿低迷している
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the embedded subject '売れ行き'.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a 〜せい clause, the subject takes が. Also, 売れ行き is the specific thing that is slumping — new, descriptive info.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a cause/reason clause would mislabel the topic and clash with the outer topic 布施は.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨が降ったせいで遅れた。
contrast_examples.en: I was late because it rained.

prompt.context_jp: 客を見送ったあと、席に戻ってこなかったのは誰か。
prompt.prompt_jp: 屋代だけ＿、客を見送ったきり、まだ席に戻ってこなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that singles out Yashiro as the only one who hasn't returned.

feedback.correct_en: 〜だけが picks Yashiro out exhaustively — he alone hasn't returned. This is classic exhaustive-listing が.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would set up a contrastive topic ('as for only Yashiro...') which doesn't fit this narrative identification.

prompt.context_jp: 理恵の個人的質問に対する屋代の返事。
prompt.prompt_jp: あなた＿は関係ありません
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks '関係' as being 'to/with you'.

feedback.correct_en: 〜に関係ある/ない is the fixed pattern for 'have to do with ~'. The に marks the party involved.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark means/location; を would make 'you' an object, which doesn't match this idiom.

contrast_examples.en: It has nothing to do with me.

prompt.context_jp: その夜、屋代は布施と連れ立って、行きつけのバー「ちちんぷいぷい」のカウンター＿腰を下ろしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: カウンター＿腰を下ろしていた
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the location where he sat down.

feedback.correct_en: 腰を下ろす takes に for the place one lowers oneself onto (a point of contact), like 座る.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks the location of an action in general, but with verbs of attaching/sitting-onto, Japanese prefers に.

prompt.context_jp: 昼間の一件＿、とっくに布施の耳にも入っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 昼間の一件＿、とっくに布施の耳にも入っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle framing 'the daytime incident' as the topic.

feedback.correct_en: The incident is already known to the reader; the narrator is now commenting on how it reached Fuse. は sets it as the familiar topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the incident as new, surprising information, which it isn't by this point.

contrast_examples.jp: その話は彼も知っていた。

prompt.context_jp: 布施：「俺もまあまあモテたけどさ」屋代について：「屋代のモテぶり＿突き抜けてたわけ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 屋代のモテぶり＿突き抜けてた
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits the implicit contrast with Fuse's own popularity.

feedback.correct_en: Fuse just said he himself was popular; now he contrasts: 'but Yashiro's popularity was on another level.' Contrastive は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just neutrally identify Yashiro's popularity as the subject, losing the contrast with Fuse's just-stated situation.

contrast_examples.jp: 僕も走れるが、彼は速い。
contrast_examples.en: I can run too, but HE is fast. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家のきっぱりとした一言。
prompt.prompt_jp: お客様＿好き嫌いはない
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle fitting this stock expression.

feedback.correct_en: 〜に好き嫌いはない means 'I have no likes/dislikes regarding X' — に marks the target domain.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 'customers' the subject of 好き嫌い itself, which doesn't match the fixed pattern.

contrast_examples.jp: 食べ物に好き嫌いはない。

contrast_examples.en: I have no complaints about work.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家の鋭い指摘。
prompt.prompt_jp: 元奥様は 家が欲しいのではなく 課長＿欲しいのです
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 課長 that mirrors the 家が contrast.

feedback.correct_en: 〜が欲しい takes が. Rie wants not the house but YOU; the exhaustive 'it's you she wants' uses が.
feedback.incorrect_en: を欲しい is ungrammatical with the 〜が欲しい pattern. は would weaken the sharp 'it's YOU' identification.

prompt.context_jp: 津田の説明：「前原が外で稼いで 僕＿家を守っています」
prompt.prompt_jp: 前原が外で稼いで 僕＿家を守っています
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 僕 that contrasts his role with his wife's.

feedback.correct_en: The two roles are explicitly contrasted: SHE earns outside, I keep house. Contrastive は on 僕 makes the pairing clear.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 僕 as new info, missing the deliberate role-contrast with 前原.

contrast_examples.jp: 兄は働き、弟は勉強する。
contrast_examples.en: The older brother works; the younger studies. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 「あぁ 以前 屋代の＿だった 理恵です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 以前 屋代の＿だった 理恵です
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that fits 'ex-wife' here.

feedback.correct_en: 以前〜だった 妻 means 'formerly his wife' — i.e., ex-wife. This is how Rie introduces herself.
feedback.incorrect_en: 娘 (daughter) and 姉 (older sister) don't match her relationship with Yashiro.

prompt.context_jp: 屋代が元妻へ丁寧に用件を尋ねる場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 本日は 弊社に どのような＿で？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the business-polite word that fits this formal inquiry.

feedback.correct_en: どのようなご用件で？ is the standard business phrase for asking a visitor's purpose.
feedback.incorrect_en: ご予定 (schedule) and ご都合 (convenience) don't fit asking why someone has come.

contrast_examples.jp: ご都合はいかがですか。

prompt.context_jp: 「私ね 4月に＿したの 2度目の夫と」
prompt.prompt_jp: 4月に＿したの 2度目の夫と
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that fits her statement about her second husband.

feedback.correct_en: She says 2回も離婚して later in the same line, confirming she divorced her second husband.
feedback.incorrect_en: 結婚 (married) or 再婚 (remarried) would contradict '2回も離婚して'.

prompt.context_jp: 布施の忠告。
prompt.prompt_jp: 20年前の＿を繰り返すなよ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun that fits '20 years ago's ___'.

feedback.correct_en: 過ちを繰り返す ('repeat the mistake') is a set collocation; Fuse warns Yashiro not to redo his marriage mistake.
feedback.incorrect_en: 喜び or 努力 don't match 繰り返すな ('don't repeat') as a warning.

prompt.context_jp: 屋代がクレーム電話に対応する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: わが社の＿をお付けいたします
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the phrase meaning 'our number-one staff'.

feedback.correct_en: To reassure the dissatisfied client he promises to assign the top performer — three軒家.
feedback.incorrect_en: 新人 (newbie) would make things worse; 課長 (manager) doesn't fit as a reassurance about the sales rep.

contrast_examples.jp: 当社ナンバーワンの営業です。

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家の助言。
prompt.prompt_jp: 家は売ればいい 復縁は＿ばいい ビシッと！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that fits her advice about remarriage.

feedback.correct_en: She tells him to refuse the reunion firmly (ビシッと). 断る fits the decisive tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 受け入れる (accept) is the opposite of her advice; 考える is too vague for ビシッと.

prompt.context_jp: 津田の花言葉の説明。
prompt.prompt_jp: 花言葉は “＿の愛”です
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that fits the balloon flower's floral meaning.

feedback.correct_en: キキョウ's floral meaning is 'eternal love' (永遠の愛), which ironically contrasts with the troubled marriage he describes.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一瞬 (an instant) and 初めて (first) don't form the standard floral phrase.

prompt.context_jp: 理恵が自嘲気味に。
prompt.prompt_jp: その上 私は＿だから
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word for 'divorced twice'.

feedback.correct_en: バツ2 is the colloquial term for someone divorced twice. Rie just said she divorced her second husband.
feedback.incorrect_en: バツ1 would mean one divorce; 独身 just means single and loses the self-deprecating specificity.

prompt.context_jp: 白洲美加が屋代課長に反論する場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural for a young employee hesitantly pushing back to her boss?

choices.text: あの～ お茶出しは 私の仕事じゃないんですけど…
あの～ お茶出しは 私の仕事ではない。

feedback.correct_en: The 〜んですけど… softener plus trailing silence lets her object while staying (barely) polite to her boss, matching her character.
feedback.incorrect_en: The flat ではない drops politeness entirely and sounds like a declaration from an equal, which doesn't fit the workplace relationship.

contrast_examples.jp: ちょっと違うんですけど…
contrast_examples.en: Um, it's a bit different... (soft pushback)

prompt.context_jp: 屋代が電話で名乗る。
prompt.prompt_en: Which opening is more natural for a manager answering a client call?

choices.text: お待たせいたしました 課長の屋代でございます
待たせたね 課長の屋代です

feedback.correct_en: お待たせいたしました + でございます is standard business phone register when addressing a client.
feedback.incorrect_en: 待たせたね is casual, as if to a friend — unthinkable to a customer who just complained.

contrast_examples.jp: お電話ありがとうございます。

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家の決めゼリフとして。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version works best as her signature boast?

choices.text: 私に売れない家はありません
私が売れない家はないです

feedback.correct_en: The 〜に〜はありません frame gives a crisp, categorical ring and lets 'house' be the topic — perfect for a tagline.
feedback.incorrect_en: The 'B' version with が and 〜ないです sounds like casual spoken grammar and loses the declarative punch.

contrast_examples.jp: 私にできないことはない。
私ができないことがない。

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家が二人の気持ちに応える場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line better captures Sangenya's blunt, parallel-structured delivery?

choices.text: 課長と庭野が私のことを女として愛していないように、私も男として課長と庭野を見つめることはありません
二人のことは好きだけど、恋愛としては見てないかな

feedback.correct_en: Sangenya speaks in flat, formal, perfectly parallel sentences. 'A' preserves her trademark style.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'B' uses casual hedging (〜かな, 見てない) that would be natural for a different character, but not for her clinical delivery.

contrast_examples.en: There is no such thing (categorical, formal).

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家が津田に尋ねる場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing fits a formal visit to a client's home?

choices.text: それは 気象予報士としての感性を高めるためですか？
それって 気象予報士の感覚磨くためなの？

feedback.correct_en: 〜ためですか？ with 感性を高める is appropriately formal and precise for a professional client interaction.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'B' uses casual 〜なの？ and 感覚磨く which is too familiar for first-visit client talk.

contrast_examples.en: Is it for the purpose of ~? (polite)
